newsitem.title: CANADA: N.American airlines ponder cargo fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: N.American airlines ponder cargo fuel surcharge.

text.p: While North American airlines have not leapt to match the fuel-inspired cargo rate increases and surcharges announced by major European carriers since Friday, most appear inclined to do so if they are sure their rivals will match.
Most of the carriers polled by Reuters said they were actively studying a surcharge.
"Quite frankly, regarding the fuel surcharge, we're going to continue watching the marketplace for a little bit," Jim Hartigan, vice-president cargo for United Airlines, told Reuters.
Vince Puccia, Northwest Airlines's director of cargo marketing, said Northwest's unit fuel cost was up over 40 percent, year over year.
"We are seriously looking at (a fuel surcharge), but we have not confirmed that we we will do it or at what rate we would do it," said Puccia.
He said that if Northwest applied a surcharge, it would need very little lead time to put it into effect, certainly not the 30 days it would take to put a normal rate increase into effect.
A U.S.-based official of a large Japanese airline also told Reuters that while no surcharge was planned on Pacific routes at present, "if market conditions permit, we could really use one."
North American carriers have raised passenger fares, in part to recover higher fuel costs.

However they have been reluctant to be first with cargo surcharges, mindful of American Airlines' experience in June when it announced a domestic cargo surcharge only to back down two weeks later after no other carriers matched it.
